purpose: Teach: 儲かっ/聴ける/リタイア/小雨/平ら/殴っ/呑ん/止めよ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんの商いが儲かった
lines.en: Your father's business did well when he was younger, Gran.
lines.style: Distant, thoughtful gaze inward. Soft voice, almost speaking to himself. Slow, measured cadence—the weight of memory. No rush.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、晩年、レコードが聴ける環境を喜ばれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes... and Grandpa was so happy in his later years when he could listen to his records, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm, affirming tone. Speaking as if coaxing a memory into focus together. Gentle lilt of tenderness, asking for agreement but already knowing the answer.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがリタイア後の人生を楽しまれた
lines.en: Your father really learned to enjoy life after he retired, Gran.
lines.style: Same distant reflection as before. Eyes half-closed, following a thread of thought. Breath shallow and thoughtful. Pause between clauses.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、小雨の日に縁側でお茶を召し上がったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa used to sit on the veranda with his tea on those light rainy days, remember? Dear?
lines.style: Soft smile in the voice. Specific, sensory detail—she's watching the memory play. Conversational, inviting him into the scene with her. Warm close on 'dear.'

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが田んぼを平らにならされた
lines.en: When he was younger, your father kept those rice paddies perfectly level, Gran.
lines.style: Voice steady but quieter now. Slower still. The cadence of someone naming difficult things with acceptance. Slight drag on the final word.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、酔って人を殴った日もあったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Though Grandpa had his darker days too—times when he'd drunk and lashed out. You remember, dear?
lines.style: No flinch in her voice. Matter-of-fact but not cold—acknowledging what was. Steady, unflinching gaze. The honesty of someone who loved him anyway.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが薬を呑んで耐えられた
lines.en: Your father took medicine to bear it all, Gran.
lines.style: Even quieter now. The voice has become a whisper almost. Resignation mixed with respect—he endured. Long, small pause before 'medicine.' Trailing away at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、晩年、無理は止めようと仰ったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And in his later years, Grandpa told you to stop pushing so hard, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Close and intimate, almost a confession. Her voice softens further. The final wisdom—his gift to Hiroshi. She waits for the weight of it to settle. Breath before 'dear.'
